candidates.title: StochasticContext is both a computed store and a config/layout echo: 5 precomputed components + 5 derived-layout scalars + 2 pass-through seeds + 1 metadata field, each exposed via a 1:1 &-getter (the nascent Switchable<T> uncertainty store)

evidence.output: 257: #[derive(Debug)] 258: pub struct StochasticContext { 259:     par_lp: PrecomputedPar, 260:     correlation: DecomposedCorrelation, 261:     opening_tree: OpeningTree, 262:     normal_lp: PrecomputedNormal, 263:     ncs_normal: PrecomputedNormal, 264:     ncs_entity_ids: Vec<EntityId>, 265:     entity_order: Box<[EntityId]>, 266:     base_seed: u64, 270:     forward_seed: Option<u64>, 271:     dim: usize, 272:     n_load_buses: usize, 273:     n_stochastic_ncs: usize, 274:     provenance: StochasticProvenance, 275: }
evidence.reading: The 13 private fields split into four roles: 5 precomputed components (par_lp, correlation, opening_tree, normal_lp, ncs_normal) that ARE the store; 5 derived-layout values (ncs_entity_ids, entity_order, dim, n_load_buses, n_stochastic_ncs) that are addressing metadata recomputable from noise_entity_order; 2 pass-through config values (base_seed, forward_seed) echoed straight from the builder args; and 1 metadata field (provenance). Every field is surfaced through a trivial &-returning getter (par()/correlation()/opening_tree()/normal()/ncs_normal()/entity_order()/... at 285-393); the only real behavior is set_solve_order (line 317), a post-construction mutation of the opening tree (two-phase init). So the Q3 answer is BOTH: a store (the precomputed infra, read by ~30 downstream files across cobre-sddp/cli, so NOT a one-consumer abstraction) fused with a parameter/layout bag (config echoed back through getters). Q4 hint: the precomputed-component group is the Switchable<T> store payload; the derived-layout group is its addressing metadata; base_seed/forward_seed are RunParams-shaped and separate from the store under the input-data-lifecycle split.

candidates.fixShape: Phase-1 destination note, NOT executed by this spec (lens Q4 is alignmentHint-only). When Part IV/V introduces the Switchable<T> uncertainty store, the precomputed-component fields become the store payload and the entity_order/dim/n_* fields its addressing metadata, while base_seed/forward_seed migrate to the RunParams half of the Model/RunParams/PolicyState split rather than being echoed through the store. No restructuring here; recorded so the alignment epic knows this struct is the carve target and the config-echo/store fusion is the seam to unpick.

None of the three is in the reserved-seam register, none carries an #[allow(dead_code)] or a reserving comment (public enum variants do not trip dead_code). By the reserved-seam register's own contract (reserved-seams-and-deferred-debt.md L11-16: a seam without an owner AND a consuming milestone 'is dead code to remove, not a seam to reserve'), these unregistered variants are dead public surface, not reserved seams.

Removing variants is a breaking change to the pub StochasticError (re-exported at lib.rs `pub use error::StochasticError`), so it rides the same 'licensed public-API break' gate the mirror applies to the superseded cut-sync public methods; the match/From surface needs no edit because no arm can match an unconstructible variant.

candidates.title: Backward season-occurrence walk is quadratic in l_state: derive_inflow_seeds restarts nth_previous_occurrence from the anchor for every k

evidence.command: git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/seeds.rs | sed -n '104,111p'; git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/season_cast/mod.rs | sed -n '615,626p;313,319p'
evidence.reading: derive_inflow_seeds calls season_occurrence(k) for k = 0..=l_state (seeds.rs:95 and the k-loop at seeds.rs:104). Each season_occurrence(k) recomputes the in_progress anchor and then calls nth_previous_occurrence(anchor, k), whose body (season_cast/mod.rs:313) walks the backward occurrence chain k steps FROM THE ANCHOR every time. So step 1..k-1 are re-walked once for every k: total walk steps are Sum(k, k=1..l_state) = l_state*(l_state+1)/2 instead of l_state. Each walk step performs three O(S) linear scans over season_map.seasons: seasons.iter().find (season_cast/mod.rs:314), previous_season_period_window's Custom-arm seasons.iter().position (season_cast/mod.rs:275+), and season_for_date (cobre-core temporal.rs:450, itself a seasons.iter().find). The redundancy is purely structural (recompute-the-prefix), independent of deck values.

candidates.mechanism: Recompute-the-prefix quadratic: season_occurrence(k) re-runs nth_previous_occurrence from the anchor for each k in the derive_inflow_seeds loop, so O(n_hydros * l_state^2 * S) backward-walk work is done where an incremental single walk (compute each occurrence once, cast at each) would be O(n_hydros * l_state * S). S is the season count (12 monthly / 52 weekly). Setup-time only: the sole production call site is StudySetup::new pre-study seeding (cobre-sddp setup/mod.rs:515, stochastic_pipeline.rs:253), run once per study, not per scenario/stage/iteration. No timing measured.
candidates.fixShape: Walk the backward season-occurrence chain once per hydro instead of restarting per k. Add a StageCalendar method (or a season_cast free helper) that, given the anchor and a max depth, yields the sequence of SeasonPeriodWindow occurrences 0..=l_state by advancing previous_season_period_window incrementally, so each occurrence and its O(S) season lookup is computed exactly once; derive_inflow_seeds then casts each returned window onto merged. This stays engine-neutral (no cut/state/Benders noun), introduces no one-consumer abstraction beyond the existing single caller, and preserves the exact walk semantics (same previous_season_period_window / season_for_date sequence) so seed values stay bit-identical.

candidates.title: derive_inflow_seeds re-scans the entire record and conditioning slices once per hydro instead of grouping by hydro_id in one pass

evidence.reading: record (the whole-study inflow_history) and conditioning (recent_observations) hold rows for ALL hydros. The hydro loop (seeds.rs:73) filters each full slice by row.hydro_id == hydro.id (seeds.rs:76 and 85) for every hydro, so each of the two slices is scanned n_hydros times. This is O(n_hydros * (|record| + |conditioning|)); a single grouping pass keyed by hydro_id built before the loop would be O(|record| + |conditioning|). record is the larger input for a real deck (every hydro's full history), so the overscan factor is the hydro count. The re-scan is structural, independent of deck values.

candidates.mechanism: Repeated full linear scan: the per-hydro .filter over record and conditioning re-reads both slices in full for each of n_hydros hydros, giving O(n_hydros * (|record| + |conditioning|)) instead of the O(|record| + |conditioning|) of a single group-by-hydro_id pass. Setup-time only (same StudySetup::new call site as the sibling candidate); no timing measured.
candidates.fixShape: Before the hydro loop, do one pass over record and one over conditioning to bucket rows by hydro_id (e.g. a HashMap<EntityId, Vec<RealizedWindow>>), then index each hydro's bucket inside the loop. Keep the existing hydros-canonical-order iteration for the returned position, and preserve the row order within each bucket so merge_layered_windows sees the same window sequence and seeds stay bit-identical. Engine-neutral, no new cross-crate dependency, single existing consumer.

candidates.title: Entity-fixture prelude (make_bus/make_stage/make_hydro/make_inflow_model/identity_correlation) duplicated near-verbatim across two inline seam test modules and the seam integration binary

evidence.command: for f in src/context.rs src/provenance.rs src/seeds.rs tests/reproducibility.rs; do echo "== $f"; git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/$f | grep -nE '^\s*fn (make_bus|make_stage|make_hydro|make_inflow_model|identity_correlation)\b'; done
evidence.reading: Five entity builders recur across three seam test regions. Bodies were read in full at baseline (context.rs:793-960, provenance.rs:35-200, tests/reproducibility.rs:1-160): make_stage (context 814 / provenance 58 / reproducibility 43), make_bus (context 839 / provenance 83 / reproducibility 30), make_hydro (context 852 / provenance 96 / reproducibility 68) and identity_correlation (context 914 / provenance 158 / reproducibility 130) are BYTE-IDENTICAL across all three files — make_hydro is the same ~50-line Hydro struct literal ending in `hydro.declare_mirror_unit_group(EntityId(0))` and the full 17-field HydroPenalties block; make_stage is the same 2024-01-01..2024-02-01 single-block Stage; identity_correlation is the same BTreeMap/spectral CorrelationModel. make_inflow_model matches verbatim between provenance (146) and reproducibility (118); context (902) is a superset that only adds std/coeffs params. seeds.rs make_hydro (198) is a FOURTH near-copy of the same Hydro literal and identical HydroPenalties block, differing only by omitting the declare_mirror_unit_group call and returning the struct directly. This is per-file fixture fragmentation with no shared harness — exactly the 'A contributor to cobre-stochastic has no template to follow' fragmentation the yardstick names (docs/design/testing-architecture.md §3.2 item 2/3 and §5.2).

candidates.fixShape: Coverage-neutral de-duplication (no test deleted, per yardstick §7): hoist the shared engine-neutral entity builders into a single test-support surface and have all three seam test regions consume it. Yardstick-canonical home (§5.2 'helpers live with the type they build') is cobre-core's `test-support` feature, since make_bus/make_stage/make_hydro/make_inflow_model/identity_correlation construct cobre-core entities (Bus/Stage/Hydro/InflowModel/CorrelationModel) — the two inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules use them via `#[cfg(test)]` and the integration binary via a `test-support` dev-dependency feature. A lighter, L1-safe alternative that stays inside this crate is a crate-internal `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))] mod test_support` in cobre-stochastic exposing the builders so tests/reproducibility.rs can reach them; it has 3+ consumers (both inline modules plus the integration binary) so it does not trip the single-consumer-abstraction guardrail, adds no engine dependency, and names no SDDP paradigm noun. Where a caller needs the extra-parameter form, keep context.rs's make_inflow_model signature (std/coeffs) as the canonical one and let the fixed-value call sites pass 30.0/vec![]. Reconcile the seeds.rs make_hydro variant (no mirror unit group) as an explicit builder option rather than a silent fourth copy.

candidates.title: Tautological equivalence test: test_season_occurrence_matches_pre_refactor_helper_sequence recomputes the same delegating arithmetic on both sides

evidence.reading: season_occurrence (615) IS the composition season_period_window -> nth_previous_occurrence -> cast over self.stages.first(). The test recomputes that exact same composition over the same inputs (expected_in_progress via season_period_window on stages[0]; the same &windows) and asserts it equals season_occurrence(...). Both sides invoke the identical delegating code path, so the assertion is f(x)==f(x); the test's own `#[allow(clippy::float_cmp)]` rationale states 'both paths run the identical arithmetic'. The 'pre-refactor helper sequence' it names is history — the refactor has landed and the helper-level tests (test_season_period_window_*, test_nth_previous_occurrence_*, test_cast_*) already cover each stage. It can only fail if someone reimplements the wrapper independently, i.e. it pins delegation as an implementation detail, adding no behavioral coverage.

candidates.fixShape: Remove the test (not a coverage reduction per yardstick §7: it asserts nothing the helper-level unit tests do not already prove, because the wrapper is a straight delegation). If the intent is to guard that the wrapper keeps delegating rather than growing an independent implementation, replace the redundant equivalence assertion with a one-line comment/pointer at season_occurrence stating that the helper-level tests are authoritative, or fold a single k-value smoke assertion into an existing calendar test. Do not keep a full 0..=3 loop whose two operands are the same call path.

positives.why: The seam's public types — StochasticContext (context.rs), StochasticError (error.rs), StochasticProvenance/ComponentProvenance (provenance.rs), DerivedInflowSeeds (seeds.rs) — carry no serde/postcard/FlatBuffers representation, and their test regions contain zero to_bits/from_bits/0x-byte-array/from_slice/round-trip assertions (grep over context.rs:793-2310 returned nothing).
